questions.prompt: You need to know where a config value is defined in a repo on your laptop, and every place it is used. You have a chat box and Claude Code. Which move fits the shape of the task?
options: Paste the config file into the chat box and ask where the value is used
Give Claude Code the goal "find where MAX_RETRIES is defined and list every place it is used" and let it search
Tell the chat box to open the repo at C:/work/app and read it
Type the config file's path into Claude Code and press enter, then read the reply
questions.explanation: Usage lives across files the tool has to find, so you hand over the destination and it picks the steps. Option A is tempting because pasting feels direct, but a chat box only sees what you pasted, so everything you left out is invisible. Option C names a path to something that cannot reach your disk at all. Option D treats Claude Code like a file viewer: you give it goals, not paths-as-questions.

questions.prompt: A colleague watches you run Claude Code and says, "so it is the same chatbot, just in a terminal." Which correction is accurate?
options: It is a bigger model than the chat box, so it answers better
Same model, different body: the terminal version can read, edit, run, and search your project; the chat box only sees what you paste
Both are completion-shaped, so it is really the same interaction
It is mainly an IDE plugin that can see your open editor tabs
questions.explanation: Same brain, different body — and the body is what lets it act on your files. Option A is the tempting one: the difference is not a smarter model, it is scope and side effects. Option C is wrong because Claude Code is goal-shaped, not completion-shaped. Option D misreads the product: it is a terminal program, not primarily an editor plugin.

questions.prompt: Your laptop is offline and the project in front of you holds credentials you are not allowed to send anywhere. You need the definition of a standard library function. What is correct?
options: Claude Code, because it runs locally in your terminal
A chat box, because you can paste in just the one function call
Neither online tool; use local docs, because Claude Code needs network access and works in your project
Claude Code, but only with plan mode switched on
questions.explanation: Claude Code sends the turn to a model over the network and operates inside your project, so an offline machine with secrets in scope is the wrong place for it. Option A is the tempting confusion: "runs in your terminal" is not the same as "runs offline." Option B fails the same network test and risks leaking whatever you paste. Option D invents a capability — plan mode restricts acting, it does not remove the need for a network.

questions.prompt: Your team cannot install Claude Code, so it uses OpenCode pointed at DeepSeek. A later lesson says "Claude Code" throughout. How should you read it?
options: Ignore it — it is about a specific product your team does not use
Read "Claude Code" as "the terminal coding agent you have installed"; the shape is the same and the brand is incidental
It applies only once your team switches to Anthropic models
It applies, but only the parts that mention the terminal
questions.explanation: The phase teaches a shape — terminal tool, goal in, route out, you approve — and treats the brand as incidental. Option A is the tempting literal reading and would throw the whole course away. Option C inverts the lesson: the model is the swappable part. Option D draws a false line; the shape, not just the terminal, is what carries over.
